title: Insomnia effector gene predictions (Watanabe et al., 2022)
bodyHtml:
This table displays results from the study:

Genome-wide meta-analysis of insomnia prioritizes genes associated with metabolic and psychiatric pathways.
Watanabe K, et al.
Nat Genet. 2022 Aug;54(8):1125-1132. doi: 10.1038/s41588-022-01124-w..
PMID: 35835914

To prioritize potentially causal genes for insomnia at independent genetically associated loci,

  • credible SNPs were defined by fine-mapping and were mapped to genes if they caused deleterious coding sequence changes or colocalized with eQTLs for the gene. Detailed evidence for these mappings is displayed in the "Credible set SNPs" row that is visible after clicking the "View" button for a row in the table below.
  • for loci that did not include credible SNPs meeting those criteria, GWAS-significant SNPs were mapped to genes if they caused deleterious coding sequence changes or colocalized with eQTLs for the gene. Detailed evidence for these mappings is displayed in the "GWAS significant SNPs" row that is visible after clicking the "View" button for a row in the table below.

Genes identified in either of these ways were termed "high-confidence" (HC) and were assigned either of two classifications, indicated in the "Classification" column:

  • Genes that were the single HC gene in a locus were classified as HC-1
  • Genes that were among multiple HC genes in a locus were classified as HC-m.

Finally, protein-protein interactions between HC-1 and HC-m gene products were investigated. Genes were classified as High-confidence prioritized genes if they were classified as HC-1 or were classified as HC-m AND their gene product interacted directly with an HC-1 gene product.

Chromatin interaction results, included in the sub-rows, were not considered in the prioritization method but are provided as potential additional supporting evidence.

Click the Research Method tab for more details.
